BBC News. JSON-LD datePublished 2026-10-24T23:50:02.059Z = 23:50 GMT Sat 24 Oct 2026. dateModified identical. Retrieved by plain curl 08:20 GMT 25 Oct. Byline: Ione Wells, reporting from Rio de Janeiro, and Patrick Jackson. Supplemented with Al Jazeera first-round copy, URL below.

SECOND URL: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/4/brazil-votes-in-deeply-polarised-election-pitting-lula-against-bolsonaro

HEADLINE: Brazil election: Voters to choose between Lula and Bolsonaro's son

POLL OPENING AND CLOSING TIMES — EXPLICITLY NOT SOURCED
I could not find poll opening or closing times for the 25 October RUNOFF in ANY approved source I was able to reach. The BBC piece does not carry them. Al Jazeera's 23 October runoff explainer does not carry them. Al Jazeera's 4 October first-round report does not carry them either. Treat the hours as NOT SOURCED and do not state them.
What IS sourced on results timing, Al Jazeera, 4 October, first round: "Results are expected within a few hours of the polls closing due to Brazil's electronic voting system."
What IS sourced on the candidates' plans, BBC: "Lula plans to be in Sao Paulo to watch the results on Sunday evening while Bolsonaro is set to be in the capital Brasilia - which is also where his father is under house arrest."
NOTE FOR THE 09:15 GMT SLOT: Brazil is on Brasilia time (UTC-3) and Brazilian polls open in the morning, local. At 09:15 GMT it will be 06:15 in Brasilia. Whatever the exact hours, Brazilian voting will NOT yet be under way at publication, unlike Serbia's, which opened at 06:00 GMT. There is no turnout figure and can be none.

ELECTORATE FIGURES (CONFLICT, do not average)
- Guardian, 24 Oct, 21:10 GMT: "Nearly 159m Brazilians will vote in the election's runoff on Sunday".
- Al Jazeera, 4 Oct, first round: "About 160 million registered voters were eligible to cast ballots in Sunday's elections".

HARD FACTS
- Lula is 80, seeking a fourth non-consecutive term, first elected in 2002/took office 2003. Flavio Bolsonaro is 45, a right-wing senator.
- Jair Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year prison sentence for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election, currently under house arrest due to ill health. Flavio has pledged to release/pardon him if elected.
- Bolsonaro came top in the first round on 4 October. BBC: "This is Bolsonaro's election to lose". Trump called it a "very big" victory.
- BBC: "Never before has a candidate who trailed after the first round managed to overturn the deficit and win in the second round."
- 33 million people did not cast a vote in the first round — the turnout gap Lula's rallies are aimed at.
- Lula's administration has accused the US of interfering in Brazil's election, an allegation Washington has called "baseless".

POLLING ON THE EVE (CONFLICT, do not average — these are different pollsters, both as published)
- CNT/MDA, released Saturday: Flavio Bolsonaro 46.3 percent, Lula 45 percent. Previous week: Bolsonaro 46.8, Lula 45.9. MDA surveyed 2,032 people from 21 to 23 October, margin of error 2.2 percentage points. (Al Jazeera)
- Datafolha, published Thursday: the pair TIED on 50 percent each, against a four-point Bolsonaro lead two weeks earlier. (Al Jazeera)
- First round, 4 October: Bolsonaro 47 percent, Lula 45 percent. (Al Jazeera)
- A survey released Wednesday found 10% of voters were still open to changing their minds. (NPR)

NAMED QUOTES
- Lula, to the crowd on Copacabana beach, Saturday: the election was a matter of "sovereignty" and people would choose between the one who kissed the Brazilian flag or the American flag. And: "We're going to win the election for one simple reason: it's true that the people want change [but] they want to move forward. They don't want to go backward."
- Flavio Bolsonaro, campaigning in Belo Horizonte, capital of Minas Gerais, in a social media video: "The time is almost here. There are only a few hours left before we shape the future of our nation for the next 30 or 40 years."
- Lula, in the first televised debate, on Bolsonaro's economic model: "Have you seen how things are going in Argentina, and are you going to keep saying that Milei is your model?" (NPR)
- Lula of Bolsonaro, per Al Jazeera: "He doesn't know what hunger is. He doesn't know Brazil."
- Flavio Bolsonaro to voters: "I will give you back the streets so that you can walk in safety." (NPR)

NOTHING IS KNOWN ABOUT THE OUTCOME.
